newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end mixed in sluggish markets.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end mixed in sluggish markets.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended mixed after a day of thin trading, driven by interest in Banco de Colombia, the nation's second largest bank in terms of assets.
Bogota's IBB index rose 0.38 percent to 870.85 on a sluggish 808 million peso volume. Medellin's IBOMED general price index dipped 0.01 percent to 13,630.76 on a 553.2 million peso trading volume.

"Speculators have shown interest in the forward operation in Banco de Colombia shares on offer at well above market value," one Bogota broker said. "But if you take out purchases of Banco de Colombia shares then trading was very thin."
Banco de Colombia registered the largest gains in both Bogota and Medellin. It recently announced a 20 peso dividend as it shared out first half profits of almost 21 billion pesos.
The forward operation unveiled last Friday involves 4.5 percent of Banco de Colombia shares, valued at more than 20 billion pesos. The deal will be completed on October 31..

"The operation saw Banco de Colombia shares being offered at 435 pesos but as investors moved to snap them up in small amounts, sellers began to hold on to them in order to speculate with the price," another Bogota trader said.
Banco de Colombia ended up 3.11 percent at 431 after a total trade of 20.5 million pesos. Its shares closed 0.95 percent in Medellin at 421 on a 10 million peso volume.
The day's other main movers were the Banco de Bogota, which closed unchanged at 5,940, on the Bogota exchange and shares in brewing giant Bavaria, up 0.02 percent at 3,950, in Medellin.
